name: Osmotic Pressure Injection System OPIS-1 'Skindeep'
description: The OPIS-1 'Skindeep' is a short-to-medium range delivery weapon developed by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals that uses focused osmotic pressure waves to drive liquid payloads through intact skin and soft tissue without penetrating the surface — no needle, no wound, no visible mark. The weapon generates a precisely calibrated pressure differential at the target surface, temporarily increasing cellular membrane permeability in a localized area and forcing a liquid payload carried in the weapon's pressurized reservoir through the skin barrier and into subcutaneous or intramuscular tissue. The payload — which can be any compound stable in liquid suspension — is delivered in approximately 0.3 seconds and leaves no external evidence of administration beyond a brief, easily-missed reddening of the skin.
legality: Prohibited (tactical variant); Licensed (medical variant, clinical use only)
specifications:
weight: 0.9 kg (unloaded)
length: 28 cm
effective range: 2–15 m (optimal delivery window)
payload reservoir: 10 mL modular cartridge (standard pharmaceutical form factor)
delivery time: 0.3 seconds (subcutaneous mode), 0.5 seconds (deep drive mode)
delivery modes: Subcutaneous (surface layer), Deep drive (intramuscular)
discharge signature: None (no sound, no visible emission, no detectable beam)
surface evidence: Localized skin reddening, fades within 4–8 minutes
power source: Micro-capacitor cell (200 deliveries per cell)
payload compatibility: Any liquid compound stable in suspension at ambient pressure
tactical_use: The 'Skindeep' is used almost exclusively in covert operations where the operator cannot afford to be identified as having discharged a weapon. Assassination, targeted incapacitation, covert sedation for abduction operations, and intelligence extraction via pharmacological means are all documented uses. The weapon's short effective range demands operators work in close proximity to targets — crowded spaces, social events, transit corridors — making social engineering skill as important as marksmanship. Counter-detection protocols for the 'Skindeep' are still underdeveloped in most security frameworks, and many deployments are never identified as weapon use at all.
cultural_context: The 'Skindeep' has generated profound unease in Meridian 88's social fabric because it collapses the boundary between medicine and violence in a way that most weapons do not. The fact that it originated as a medical device — and that its medical variant remains legally available — means that trust in clinical pharmaceutical delivery has been measurably eroded in communities aware of the weapon's existence. Some districts have developed informal protocols around receiving any medical treatment from unknown practitioners. The weapon is particularly associated with Lazarus Pharmaceuticals' corporate intelligence division, which officially denies its existence, and with a loose network of freelance pharmacological operators known in the underground as 'dosers.'
known_users: Tessera Corponation executive protection details (counter-dose detection protocols)
Intelligence extraction specialists working for multiple corporate clients
story_hooks: A senior Meridian 88 council member collapsed during a public address — medical examination shows a compound in their bloodstream that doesn't match any licensed Lazarus Pharmaceuticals payload. Someone synthesized a new cartridge, and the council member's staff wants to know what was delivered before the effects become permanent.

A doser operating in the Palladian Quarter has been selling a payload that induces total, specific memory loss of the past 72 hours — no other cognitive effects, no physical symptoms. The compound shouldn't exist. Someone wants to know who's manufacturing it and why.

The players discover that the social event they've been hired to attend has been identified as a 'Skindeep operation' — someone in the room is planning to dose a target, and the players don't know who the operator is, who the target is, or what's in the cartridge.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals is quietly recalling a specific medical delivery device model — the same form factor as the 'Skindeep.' They claim a manufacturing defect, but the recall notice was issued forty minutes after a foreign diplomat died in a Meridian 88 hotel.
